text.p: Following are some key facts about Ecuador, where Congress voted late on Thursday to oust President Abdala Bucaram.
Congress appointed Fabian Alarcon, the legislative speaker, to be president, while Vice President Rosalia Arteaga also staked a claim to the post.

Bucaram, a lawyer and former athlete, defiantly pledged to remain in the palace and contest the legislature's vote. He won a four-year term on a populist ticket in July 1996 elections, becoming Ecuador's fifth democratically elected president since six years of military rule ended in 1979.

The Andean exporter of oil and bananas was a member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) but withdrew in 1992 to allow it to increase crude output unfettered by the group's quotas.

Bucaram's predecessor and opponent, conservative architect Sixto Duran Ballan, who ruled from 1992-1996, was obstructed in his free market plans by a combative Congress and became a lame duck leader long before his term ended.

Congress' ousting of Bucaram on grounds of mental incompetence came after the country was shut down on Wednesday and Thursday by a massive 48-hour nationwide general strike to protest government austerity measures introduced in January.

The measures included hikes of more than 200 percent on electricity and gas rates and a 60 percent rise in bus fares. The centrepiece of Bucaram's economic programme was the introduction of "Convertibility", pegging the value of the local sucre currency to the dollar, planned for the middle of this year.
About 40 percent of the country's population of 11.7 million is indigenous and about 50 percent of Ecuadoreans live in poverty, 30 percent living in extreme poverty.
Key facts:
- Congress is a unicameral chamber with 82 members.
- Bucaram was elected with 54.5 percent of the vote on July 7, 1996, while Jaime Nebot, the Social Christian candidate, won 45.5 percent.
- The government comprises 16 ministers and the vice president.
- Official name: Republic of Ecuador.
- Area: 104,500 sq mile (270,670 sq km)
- Capital: Quito, which has 1.5 million inhabitants.
- Ecuador borders on Colombia in the north, Peru in the south and the Pacific Ocean to the west.
- Currency: Sucre, which is worth 3,715 per dollar.
- Official language: Spanish.
- Time - GMT minus five hours.
- The country is a member of the Andean Pact, the Rio Group, the Non-Aligned Group, United Nations and the Organisation of American States.
- Population: 11.7 million.
- Population growth is 2.4 percent annually.
- Fertility rate: 3.6 children per woman.
- Mortality rate: 36.9 per 1,000.
- Life expectancy: 70 years.
- Rate of illiteracy: 37 percent.
- Religions: 90 percent is Catholic and the remainder is mainly Protestant.
- Income per head: $1,605.
- 1996 inflation rate: 25.5 percent.
- 1995 economic growth rate: 2.3 percent.
- Main exports: oil, bananas, shrimp and coffee.
